newsitem.title: USA: Huntway Partners bankruptcy plan approved.
newsitem.headline: Huntway Partners bankruptcy plan approved.

text.p: Huntway Partners LP said on Thursday its prepackaged reorganization plan has been confirmed by U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Delaware.

The plan, filed on Nov. 12, had been pre-approved four of the company's five senior lenders, its junior lenders, warrant holders and 98.6 percent of its unitholders. The fifth senior lender agreed to a restructuring just before the plan was confirmed by bankruptcy court, Huntway said in a statement.
"Confirmation of our prepackaged plan concludes a nearly two-year effort to reduce indebtedness and increase partners' capital," said Juan Forster, chief executive officer.

In the restructuring, Huntway said its total debt, including accrued interest, will decrease by $71 million. Total units outstanding will increase by about 13.8 million to a total just over 25.3 million.
Trade suppliers and creditors who were paid under normal terms throughout the bankruptcy process, and did not feel any effect from the restructuring, Huntway said.
Huntway estimates its per unit book value will increase from a negative $2.60 at September 30 to slightly over $1.50 at December 31.

Huntway plans to issue $23.5 million in new 12 percent senior secured notes and $2.07 million in new 12 percent junior notes. It also will issue just under 13.8 million units. All the new notes will bear interest from January 1, 1996 with the first interest payment due on March 31, 1997.

The company's $17.5 million debtor-in-possession letter of credit will terminate, and it will be replaced with a new $17.5 million letter of credit facility to be used primarily for collateralizing crude purchases.
Huntway Partners, L.P. owns and operates, two oil refineries at Wilmington and Benicia, California. A third refinery, at Coolidge, Arizona, has been shut down since 1993.
